paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: Suppose your university is conducting a survey to collect students’ opinions of online classes. You are to write a response to the survey about their advantages and disadvantages, and what improvements can be made. You will have 30 minutes for the task. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：假设您的大学正在进行一项调查，以收集学生对在线课程的意见。您要写一份调查回复，说明它们的优点和缺点，以及可以进行哪些改进。您将有 30 分钟的时间来完成该任务。您应该写至少 120 个字但不超过 180 个字。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，有一段有十个空格。您需要从文章后面的单词库中给出的选项列表中为每个空白选择一个单词。在做出选择之前仔细阅读该段落。银行中的每个选择都由一个字母标识。请在答题卡 2 上的每个项目上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。您不得多次使用银行中的任何单词。

paragraphs.sourceText: Morocco is responding to increasing energy demands by setting up one of the largest solar plants in the world.
paragraphs.translationZh: 摩洛哥正在通过建立世界上最大的太阳能发电厂之一来应对日益增长的能源需求。

paragraphs.sourceText: The Noor solar power station is 26 in the city of Ouarzazate and, once completed, will generate 580 million watts of electricity. The World Bank estimates it will serve 1.1 million people. It’s 27 to be completed soon.
paragraphs.translationZh: 努尔太阳能电站位于瓦尔扎扎特市，建成后将发电5.8亿瓦。世界银行估计它将为 110 万人提供服务。预计很快就会完成。

paragraphs.sourceText: Morocco’s current energy comes 28 from imports. The nation hopes to get 50 percent of its energy from renewable sources by 2030. With demand for energy 29 at an annual rate of 7 percent, the new solar plant could be a 30 part of that goal.
paragraphs.translationZh: 摩洛哥目前的能源主要来自进口。该国希望到 2030 年，50% 的能源来自可再生能源。随着能源需求以每年 7% 的速度增长，新的太阳能发电厂可能成为实现这一目标的关键部分。

paragraphs.sourceText: “This makes Morocco a big 31 in the field of solar energy in the Arab region and the African continent. It could also be a forerunner for many other countries in the world that 32 on foreign imports of energy,” said Ali Hajji, a solar energy specialist and engineering professor.
paragraphs.translationZh: “这使得摩洛哥成为阿拉伯地区和非洲大陆太阳能领域的先驱。它也可能成为世界上许多依赖外国进口能源的国家的先行者，”太阳能专家兼工程学教授阿里·哈吉(Ali Hajji)说。

paragraphs.sourceText: Experts believe that the Middle East and North Africa have huge 33 for solar energy projects. This is partly because of adequate sunlight and partly because technology has become more 34 in the region.
paragraphs.translationZh: 专家认为，中东和北非地区太阳能项目潜力巨大。这部分是因为充足的阳光，部分是因为该地区的技术变得更加便宜。

paragraphs.sourceText: “The last few years have seen a realization of 35 how competitive solar technologies can be,” said Michael Taylor, a senior analyst at the International Renewable Energy Agency.
paragraphs.translationZh: 国际可再生能源机构高级分析师迈克尔·泰勒表示：“过去几年我们已经认识到太阳能技术的竞争力。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: New Formula One Chief Hopes to Grab Americans’ Attention
paragraphs.translationZh: 新任一级方程式主席希望引起美国人的注意

paragraphs.sourceText: A) For the past four decades, the leader of Formula One car racing, one of the biggest annual sporting series in the world, was Bernie Ecclestone, a former motorcycle parts dealer who built it into an international presence essentially on his own.
paragraphs.translationZh: 答）在过去的四十年里，世界上最大的年度体育系列赛之一一级方程式赛车的领导者是伯尼·埃克莱斯顿（Bernie Ecclestone），他是一位前摩托车零部件经销商，基本上是靠自己的力量将一级方程式赛车打造成国际影响力。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) A skilled backroom operator who speaks without a filter, Ecclestone said often that in his opinion, the sport was at its best when he was allowed to act as “a dictator.”
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 埃克莱斯顿是一位熟练的幕后操作员，说话不带任何过滤器，他经常说，在他看来，当他被允许扮演“独裁者”时，这项运动处于最佳状态。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) Yet now the dictator is gone. After an American company, Liberty Media, acquired the Formula One competition recently, Chase Carey — a former executive with Fox Broadcasting Company and DirecTV who by his own admission is not a fierce racing fan — was named to replace Ecclestone and to try to renovate the organization’s management, reach and ambition.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 然而现在独裁者已经走了。美国公司 Liberty Media 最近收购了一级方程式赛车赛事后，福克斯广播公司和 DirecTV 的前高管蔡斯·凯里 (Chase Carey) 被任命接替埃克莱斯顿，并试图革新该组织的管理、影响力和雄心。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) Among the goals, Carey said in an interview on Tuesday, is one that just about every global sport seems interested in chasing: increasing interest in the United States. “People have said we’re going to ‘Americanize’ it,” Carey said. “And we’re not going to do that totally. But realistically, there are some elements of Americanization that the sport could use.”
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 凯里在周二的采访中表示，目标之一是几乎所有全球体育运动都有兴趣追逐的目标：增加对美国的兴趣。 “人们说我们要把它‘美国化’，”凯里说。 “我们不会完全这样做。但实际上，这项运动可以利用美国化的一些元素。”

paragraphs.sourceText: E) While Formula One commands enormous audiences throughout much of the world, many American sports fans know it as that other motorsport, the one that is not Nascar (纳斯卡车赛). Formula One teams race far more technologically advanced vehicles around tracks all over the world — in magnificent events in places like Malaysia, Monaco, Singapore and the United Arab Emirates, and on tradition-rich tracks like Silverstone in England and Monza in Italy too.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 虽然一级方程式赛车在世界大部分地区拥有大量观众，但许多美国体育迷将其视为另一种赛车运动，而不是纳斯卡（纳斯卡车赛）。一级方程式车队驾驶着技术更加先进的车辆在世界各地的赛道上比赛——在马来西亚、摩纳哥、新加坡和阿拉伯联合酋长国等地的盛大赛事中，以及在英国银石赛道和意大利蒙扎等传统丰富的赛道上进行比赛。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) The series has an annual race in Austin, Texas. But within “a few years,” Carey said, he plans to bring another to a destination American city, like New York, Los Angeles, Miami or Las Vegas. Carey’s ambitious plan is two-fold: first, change the business model of Formula One, which he said was a “one-man show” under Ecclestone that had a largely narrow vision when it came to negotiating partnership deals; and second, alter the way fans experience the sport, both in person and remotely, so that connections between the audience and people within the series are easier to make.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 该系列赛每年在德克萨斯州奥斯汀举行一场比赛。但凯里说，“几年内”，他计划将另一个带到美国目的地城市，如纽约、洛杉矶、迈阿密或拉斯维加斯。凯里雄心勃勃的计划有两个方面：首先，改变一级方程式的商业模式，他说这是埃克莱斯顿领导下的一场“独角戏”，在谈判合作伙伴关系时视野非常狭窄；其次，改变一级方程式赛车的商业模式。其次，改变球迷亲自和远程体验这项运动的方式，以便观众和系列赛中的人之间更容易建立联系。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) Increased digital access for fans, a more behind-the-scenes experience for broadcast viewers and innovation in areas like virtual reality — what is it like to speed around a track inside a Ferrari? — are among the possibilities. “The sport has clearly been underserved,” Carey said. “It doesn’t do anything digitally. There’s no marketing. It doesn’t tell any stories. The goal in this is to make the fans connect to the live experience as much as possible, and the tools you have to do that, we’re not using at all.”
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 增加了车迷的数字访问，为广播观众提供了更多的幕后体验，以及虚拟现实等领域的创新——驾驶法拉利在赛道上飞驰是什么感觉？ - 都是可能性之一。 “这项运动显然没有得到充分的服务，”凯里说。 “它没有以数字方式做任何事情。没有营销。它不讲任何故事。这样做的目标是让粉丝尽可能多地连接到现场体验，而我们根本没有使用为此而必须使用的工具。”

paragraphs.sourceText: H) The larger question, though, is a familiar one: Is there room for Formula One in the ever-crowded sports landscape of the United States? Opinions vary, particularly because viewing habits among consumers continue to evolve. John Bloom, a professor at Shippensburg University who has studied American sports history, said the biggest challenge for any sport trying to increase its presence in the United States was framing itself in a way that had lasting appeal. “Sports generally become popular in some way because they establish a narrative,” Bloom said. “When I think of motorsports in the U.S., what we all think of is Nascar, and the narrative of Nascar is sort of rural, white, working-class Americans, mostly in the South, connecting with the atmosphere of those races. That’s the narrative. When I think of the narrative of Formula One, it’s a very different kind of audience.”
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 不过，更大的问题是一个熟悉的问题：在美国日益拥挤的体育界中，一级方程式赛车是否有空间？人们的观点各不相同，尤其是因为消费者的观看习惯不断变化。研究美国体育史的西彭斯堡大学教授约翰·布鲁姆表示，对于任何试图扩大在美国影响力的体育运动来说，最大的挑战是以一种具有持久吸引力的方式来塑造自己。 “体育运动通常会以某种方式变得流行，因为它们建立了一种叙事，”布鲁姆说。 “当我想到美国的赛车运动时，我们都会想到纳斯卡，而纳斯卡的叙述有点像美国农村、白人、工人阶级（主要是在南方），与这些比赛的氛围联系在一起。这就是叙述。当我想到一级方程式的叙述时，这是一群非常不同的观众。”

paragraphs.sourceText: I) That difference, Carey said, is significant. While some might immediately link Formula One to Nascar in terms of American growth, Carey said Formula One’s brand research had indicated there was very little crossover; rather, Formula One fans generally cite other so-called elite events, like Wimbledon or the Ryder Cup, as competitions they enjoy. “Other than they’re both cars, the Nascar fan base is a very different fan base,” Carey said. “It’s a very regional fan base. Formula One is a global, famous brand of stars. These are machines that shock and awe you.”
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 凯里说，这种差异是显着的。虽然有些人可能会立即将一级方程式赛车与纳斯卡赛车在美国的增长方面联系起来，但凯里表示一级方程式赛车的品牌研究表明两者之间几乎没有交叉；相反，一级方程式赛车迷通常会引用其他所谓的精英赛事，例如温布尔登或莱德杯，作为他们喜欢的比赛。 “除了它们都是赛车之外，纳斯卡的粉丝群是一个非常不同的粉丝群，”凯里说。 “这是一个非常区域性的粉丝群。一级方程式赛车是一个全球知名的明星品牌。这些机器会让你感到震惊和敬畏。”

paragraphs.sourceText: J) Carey’s background is in deal making and innovation. At Fox Broadcasting Company, he was a top advisor for years, known for his skill in helping to lead the launch of company into sports, as well as the start of Fox News Channel. After going to DirecTV, he positioned the satellite provider as a mainstream option in millions of households.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) Carey 的背景是交易和创新。在福克斯广播公司，他担任了多年的高级顾问，以帮助领导公司进军体育领域以及福克斯新闻频道的创办而闻名。加入 DirecTV 后，他将卫星提供商定位为数百万家庭的主流选择。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) Now, after Liberty Media paid $4.4 billion to acquire Formula One, he is charged with making the investment pay off. “I think they can build Formula One in the U.S.,” said Patrick Crakes, an executive at InVivo Media Group who spent 25 years at Fox Broadcasting Company before leaving in 2016 as a senior manager at Fox Sports. “People don’t work on their cars anymore. They don’t want that connection anymore. It’s about technology and pushing the limits. It’s about speed, danger and risk. And Formula One has that more than any other racing series.”
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 现在，在 Liberty Media 斥资 44 亿美元收购一级方程式赛车之后，他负责让投资获得回报。 InVivo Media Group 高管帕特里克·克拉克斯 (Patrick Crakes) 表示：“我认为他们可以在美国建立一级方程式赛车。”他在福克斯广播公司 (Fox Broadcasting Company) 工作了 25 年，并于 2016 年离职，担任福克斯体育 (Fox Sports) 高级经理。 “人们不再在他们的汽车上工作。他们不再想要这种联系。这是关于技术和挑战极限。这是关于速度、危险和风险。而一级方程式赛车比任何其他赛车系列都更具有这一点。”

paragraphs.sourceText: L) That is what hooked Carey, and he said he thought his experience was not unusual. He recalled attending Formula One’s Monaco race last year and being overwhelmed by the ceremony leading up to the event, the way the race charmed the city for days ahead of the start. In his mind it felt like a Super Bowl (超级碗橄榄球赛).
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 这正是凯里着迷的原因，他说他认为自己的经历并不罕见。他回忆起去年参加一级方程式摩纳哥站比赛的情景，并被赛事前的仪式所震撼，比赛在开始前几天就让这座城市着迷。在他看来，这感觉就像一场超级碗锦标赛。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) Then, on race day, he watched as the cars rocketed out of a tunnel and went screaming toward a tight turn with the city’s harbor and the Mediterranean Sea in the background framing the scene. He was fascinated. “You can’t help but be awed,” he said, “and I think that feeling can be translated to the viewer.”
paragraphs.translationZh: M) 然后，在比赛当天，他看着汽车冲出隧道，尖叫着驶向急转弯，背景是城市的港口和地中海。他很着迷。 “你会情不自禁地感到敬畏，”他说，“我认为这种感觉可以传达给观众。”

paragraphs.sourceText: N) He added: “The broader sport is a little too inward-looking, and we need to be more open. In some ways, I’m glad to be coming from the outside. The guys who are in the sport forever are sitting there saying: ‘We can’t do that. We can’ t do that because it’s never been done that way.’ ”
paragraphs.translationZh: N）他补充道：“更广泛的运动有点过于内向，我们需要更加开放。在某些方面，我很高兴来自外部。永远参与这项运动的人坐在那里说：‘我们不能那样做。我们不能那样做，因为从来没有这样做过。’”

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. Chase Carey believes greater use should be made of digital technology to make Formula One more accessible to its fans.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 蔡斯·凯里 (Chase Carey) 认为，应该更多地利用数字技术，让粉丝更容易接触一级方程式赛车。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. Chase Carey was deeply impressed by the ceremony preceding last year’s Monaco race.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. Chase Carey 对去年摩纳哥站比赛前的仪式印象深刻。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. One of Chase Carey’s goals is to make Formula One more appealing to Americans.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 蔡斯·凯里的目标之一是让一级方程式赛车对美国人更具吸引力。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. A former motorbike parts dealer led Formula One for the past forty years.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 一位前摩托车零件经销商在过去四十年里一直领导一级方程式赛车。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. Chase Carey thought the audience of Formula One could be made to share his feeling about the race.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 蔡斯·凯里 (Chase Carey) 认为可以让一级方程式观众分享他对比赛的感受。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. Chase Carey used to serve as a top advisor for a major broadcasting company.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 蔡斯·凯里 (Chase Carey) 曾担任一家大型广播公司的高级顾问。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. Chase Carey intends to make connections easier between the audience and the Formula One racers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 蔡斯·凯里 (Chase Carey) 打算让观众和一级方程式赛车手之间的联系变得更容易。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. The new leader of Formula One admitted he was not super interested in car racing.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 一级方程式新任领导人承认他对赛车不太感兴趣。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. People’s opinions differ as to whether Formula One can be promoted in the U.S.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 对于一级方程式能否在美国推广，人们意见不一。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. Compared with other racing series, Formula One focuses more on speed and involves more danger.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 与其他赛车系列相比，一级方程式赛车更注重速度，也更危险。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：本节有 2 段。每段文章后面都有一些问题或未完成的陈述。每个选项都有四个选项，标记为 A)、B)、C) 和 D)。您应该决定最佳选择，并在答题卡 2 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Supermarkets have long been suffering as one of the thinnest-margined businesses in existence and one of the least-looked-forward-to places to work or visit. For more than a decade, they have been under attack from e-commerce giants, blamed for making Americans fat, and accused of contributing to climate change.
paragraphs.translationZh: 超市长期以来一直是利润最薄的企业之一，也是最不受期待的工作或旅游场所之一。十多年来，它们一直受到电子商务巨头的攻击，被指责让美国人发胖，并被指责加剧了气候变化。

paragraphs.sourceText: Supermarkets can technically be defined as giants housing 15,000 to 60,000 different products. The revolutionary idea of a self-service grocery, where people could hunt and gather food from aisles rather than asking a clerk to fetch items from behind a counter, first came about in America. There is some debate about which was the very first, but over the years a consensus has built around King Kullen Supermarket, founded in New York in 1930.
paragraphs.translationZh: 从技术上讲，超市可以定义为拥有 15,000 至 60,000 种不同产品的巨型超市。自助杂货店的革命性想法首先出现在美国，人们可以在过道上寻找和收集食物，而不是让店员从柜台后面取货。关于哪家是第一个存在一些争议，但多年来，围绕 1930 年在纽约成立的 King Kullen 超市达成了共识。

paragraphs.sourceText: For some 300 years, Americans had fed themselves from small stores and public markets. Shopping for food involved mud, noisy chickens, clouds of flies, nasty smells, bargaining, and getting short-changed. The supermarket imitated the Fordist factory, with its emphasis on efficiency and standardization, and reimagined it as a place to buy food. Supermarkets may not feel cutting-edge now, but they were a revolution in distribution at the time. They were such strange marvels that, on her first official state visit to the United States in 1957, Queen Elizabeth II insisted on an impromptu (即兴的) tour of a suburban-Maryland Giant Food.
paragraphs.translationZh: 大约 300 年来，美国人一直靠小商店和公共市场吃饭。购买食物涉及泥土、吵闹的鸡、成群的苍蝇、难闻的气味、讨价还价和被骗。这家超市模仿了福特工厂，强调效率和标准化，并将其重新定位为购买食品的场所。超市现在可能感觉不太先进，但在当时却是分销领域的一场革命。这些都是如此奇怪的奇迹，以至于在 1957 年女王伊丽莎白二世首次对美国进行正式国事访问时，她坚持要即兴参观马里兰州郊区的一家巨型食品公司。

paragraphs.sourceText: The typical supermarket layout has barely changed over the past 90 years. Most stores open with flowers, fruit and vegetables at the front as a breath of freshness to arouse our appetite. Meanwhile, they keep the milk, eggs, and other daily basics all the way back so you’ll travel through as much of the store as possible, and be tempted along the way.
paragraphs.translationZh: 过去 90 年来，典型的超市布局几乎没有变化。大多数商店开门时都会在门前摆上鲜花、水果和蔬菜，给人一种清新的气息，勾起我们的食欲。与此同时，他们会一直保留牛奶、鸡蛋和其他日常必需品，这样你就可以尽可能多地逛商店，并沿途受到诱惑。

paragraphs.sourceText: In the early days, as the supermarket multiplied, so did our suspicion of it. We have long feared that this “revolution in distribution” uses corporate black magic on our appetite. The book The Hidden Persuaders, published in 1957, warned that supermarkets were putting women in a “hypnoidal trance (催眠恍惚状态),” causing them to wander aisles bumping into boxes and “picking things off shelves at random.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 早期，随着超市的增多，我们对它的怀疑也随之增加。我们长期以来一直担心这场“分配革命”会利用企业黑魔法来影响我们的胃口。 1957 年出版的《隐藏的劝说者》一书警告说，超市让女性处于“催眠恍惚状态”，导致她们在过道中徘徊，撞到箱子，并“随意从货架上拿东西”。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: The traditional school year, with three months of vacation every summer, was first implemented when America was an agricultural society and the summer months were needed for farm work. Since then, we’ve completely changed as a nation. Students no longer spend summers farming, but they aren’t in school, either. The average American student receives 13 weeks off from school each calendar year — with about 11 of those during the summer. Few other countries have more than seven weeks off in a school calendar.
paragraphs.translationZh: 传统学年每年夏天有三个月的假期，最初是在美国还是农业社会、需要暑假从事农活的时候实行的。从那时起，我们作为一个国家彻底改变了。学生们不再在暑假里务农，但他们也不上学了。美国学生平均每年有 13 周的假期，其中大约 11 周是在夏季。很少有其他国家的学校假期超过七周。

paragraphs.sourceText: With the US lagging behind countries in academics, it’s time to consider year-round schooling. One benefit of this change is that students will not fall victim to the “summer slide,” or the well-documented phenomenon where students forget some of the knowledge they have acquired when too much time is taken off from school. Decades of research shows that it can take from 8 to 13 weeks at the beginning of every school year for students to get back to where they were before the summer holiday.
paragraphs.translationZh: 由于美国在学术方面落后于其他国家，是时候考虑全年教育了。这一变化的好处之一是，学生不会成为“夏季滑坡”的受害者，即学生因休学时间过长而忘记所学知识的现象。数十年的研究表明，学生在每个学年开始时可能需要 8 到 13 周的时间才能恢复到暑假前的状态。

paragraphs.sourceText: But year-round schooling isn’t just about academics. Teachers and students experience a closer relationship in year-round schools than they do in traditional schools and, in the absence of any long-term break, students do not feel detached from the school environment. These closer bonds and greater attachment pay off. Research shows that students in year-round schools are more self-confident and feel more positive about their schooling experience.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但全年学校教育不仅仅关乎学术。与传统学校相比，在全年制学校中，教师和学生的关系更加密切，并且在没有长期休息的情况下，学生不会感到与学校环境脱离。这些更紧密的联系和更强的依恋得到了回报。研究表明，全年制学校的学生更加自信，对自己的学习经历更加积极。

paragraphs.sourceText: But don’t kids need time to relax? Some childhood development experts believe that time off from school is vital to healthy development as kids are not designed to spend so much of their time inside classrooms and the summer break provides a perfect opportunity to get outside. The problem with this argument is that most children aren’t playing outside or even spending time with other kids. While some children visit summer camps, most stay at home, watching TV or playing games on electronic devices, which hardly benefits them.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但孩子们不需要时间放松吗？一些儿童发展专家认为，离开学校的时间对于健康发展至关重要，因为孩子们生来不会在教室里花太多时间，而暑假提供了一个外出的绝佳机会。这种观点的问题在于，大多数孩子不会在外面玩耍，甚至不会花时间与其他孩子在一起。虽然有些孩子参加夏令营，但大多数孩子都呆在家里看电视或玩电子设备，这对他们来说几乎没有好处。

paragraphs.sourceText: The US has changed from a farming economy to a knowledge- and innovation-based economy, so it makes sense for the school year to change as well.
paragraphs.translationZh: 美国已经从农业经济转变为知识和创新型经济，因此学年的改变也是有意义的。
